details: The Democratic Party has secured control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the recent U.S. midterm elections. This "blue wave" has raised concerns within the cryptocurrency industry about potentially tougher regulations and increased scrutiny from Congress. There is speculation that Senator Elizabeth Warren, a known critic of the crypto sector, may chair the Senate Banking Committee, advocating for stricter rules and expanded SEC oversight. This political shift could delay pro-industry legislation and lead to congressional investigations into crypto businesses.
title: Democrats' Midterm Victory Sparks Fears of Stricter Crypto Regulation

details: Following last week's massive $6.3 billion Binance hack, which the FBI has attributed to a North Korea-linked group, insurers are reportedly increasing their scrutiny of crypto companies' security measures. Underwriters are expected to thoroughly probe clients' vulnerabilities to similar attacks when processing new or renewed coverage. Experts indicate that no existing crypto insurance policy could cover a loss of this magnitude, suggesting tougher questions and potential new exclusions for crypto firms.
title: Binance $6.3 Billion Heist Leads to Tighter Scrutiny by Insurers

details: October's Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) report showed a significant gain of 165,000 jobs, far exceeding forecasts, and the unemployment rate dropped to 4.1%. This robust labor market data strengthens the case for the Federal Reserve to implement a rate hike in December. Traders are now pricing in a 79% chance of a 25-basis-point hike on December 9. Higher interest rates typically increase borrowing costs and reduce market liquidity, making risk assets like cryptocurrencies less attractive and reinforcing a bearish bias.
title: Strong US Jobs Report Fuels Fed Rate Hike Expectations, Weighing on Crypto

details: The financial markets have experienced a deep sell-off in the AI trade and broader technology stocks, with the Nasdaq Composite entering correction territory. Concerns are rising that the Democratic control of Congress could lead to increased regulation and a slowdown in the crucial AI data-center buildout. This widespread risk-off sentiment in traditional equity markets is generating pressure across the crypto sector, as Bitcoin's correlation with the S&P 500 remains elevated.
title: AI-Driven Tech Sell-off Broadens, Impacts Risk Appetite

details: The U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has designated eight Canada-based Money Services Businesses (MSBs) under Executive Order 13902. These businesses are accused of operating in the digital asset sector of the Iranian economy, facilitating transactions with sanctioned Iranian digital asset exchanges, entities linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), and even drug traffickers. Six TRON addresses associated with four of the designated entities were also listed. This highlights ongoing efforts to combat illicit financial activities using cryptocurrencies.
title: OFAC Sanctions Canadian MSBs for Operating in Iran's Digital Asset Sector
